title: Shams disappears
hookLine: Shams leaves, returns, and vanishes for good around 1247, and Rumi's grief becomes poetry

lines: GRIEF THAT HAS TO GO SOMEWHERE.
cards: You've probably seen someone grieve out loud. Not quietly, not politely. The friend who played the same song forty times after the breakup.
The widower who talked about his wife to everyone at the grocery store. Grief that has to go somewhere. Rumi's life had just been turned upside down by a friend.
Then the friend left. Then he came back. Then, one winter night around 1247, he was gone, and nobody ever saw him again.
And the respectable scholar did something no one in Konya expected. He began to sing.

teach.b: Rumi's students resented Shams for taking their teacher away. After about sixteen months, in early 1246, Shams slipped out of Konya and went to Damascus. Rumi was desolate.
He sent his son Sultan Walad all the way to Syria to bring him back, and Shams came. For a while things were good.

teach.h: BROUGHT BACK, THEN GONE FOR GOOD.
teach.b: Then the resentment returned, and around December 1247 Shams vanished for good.
What happened? Honestly, nobody knows. A later story says he was murdered, and even names one of Rumi's own sons as involved.
Historians such as Franklin Lewis doubt that story, and there's no proof. Other accounts say he simply left, as he'd left places all his life. Rumi went looking.

He traveled to Damascus and searched the streets. Somewhere in the search, the tradition says, he stopped looking outside. He began to feel that what he loved in Shams was already speaking through him.
And he wrote. Out of this loss came a huge collection of lyric poems, thousands of them; tradition says many were composed aloud, some while he turned to music.

teach.h: POEMS SIGNED WITH HIS FRIEND'S NAME.
teach.b: It's called the Divan of Shams of Tabriz, because at the end of many poems, where a poet usually signs his own name, Rumi signed his friend's. He gave his poems away to the one he'd lost. His grief didn't go quiet.
It became music: the grief sang.

how: Readers of Rumi usually meet this grief through the Divan of Shams of Tabriz, his collection of lyric poems, many of which close with Shams's name where a poet would sign his own.

o: Rumi sending Shams away after his students complained
Shams leaving Konya to found his own school
Rumi's friend vanishing for good, around 1247

games.q: what goes with what — tap the pairs.
p: where Shams went, and was found
poems signed with his friend's name

s: a later story says so, but there's no proof, and historians such as Franklin Lewis doubt it. nobody knows.
Rumi signed many poems with Shams's name
where a poet usually signs his own name, Rumi put his friend's.
he left for Damascus, was brought back by Rumi's son, and then vanished for good.

games.q: you're Rumi. your friend has fled to Damascus after your students drove him off. what do you do?
o: let him go; your students were right.
send your son to Syria to bring him back.
go back to teaching as if nothing happened.
games.why: he sent his son Sultan Walad all the way to Damascus, and Shams came back, for a while.

practice: Let one person come to mind who's gone: someone who died, moved away, or drifted off.

Find one line for them, not poetry, maybe a thing they used to say, what you'd tell them now, or just their name and a color, and say it inside or write it down. Let the missing be there without fixing it.

wordCard.voice: Shams disappears. Around 1247 Rumi's friend vanished for good, and Rumi's grief poured out as thousands of poems signed with Shams's name. Today's word.

orig.note: Persian: a collected book of poems. the Divan-e Shams-e Tabrizi is Rumi's lyric collection.

carryVoice: Your line: the grief sang. Many of those poems still carry his friend's name. See you tomorrow.
